POSE-PLATE REGENERATION 2026-11-08 (high-five geometry cure): the painted pose plates' raised arms disagreed with the rig pose spec (DetectivePair.tsx @ 9e49da3) — in the old high-five plates the anchor hand was a flat rig-colour disc (242,196,154), not painted skin, the arm rose from the wrong shoulder line, and a duplicate base-position front hand remained. All six arm-pose plates were regenerated as composites of the cured parts at the pose-spec angles (high-five: arm-front rotated about its pivot by the harness angle, hand segment extended along the arm axis so the painted palm lands on HIGH_FIVE_CONTACT; celebrate/clap: parts at CELEBRATE/CLAP spec angles, arms behind/over torso in rig draw order). Measured on the shipped plates (harness skin band, >=40px cluster within 30 vb): Holmes high-five palm (98.89,25.36) vb, 0.37 vb from (99,25), 229 px; Watson (15.44,20.91), 0.45 vb from (15,21), 224 px. Celebrate palms 0.39-0.90 vb from rig targets; clap palms 0.29-0.36 vb. Glass: high-five and Holmes celebrate/clap carry zero pale-lens px (glass = null); Watson celebrate carries the prop glass at the rig position. NOTE: the parts-assembly palm number is bounded by rigid-arm geometry — the arm-front part's palm radius (26.6 vb Holmes) is shorter than the contact radius (39.1 vb), so a pure rotation assembly lands ~7.3 rig px short regardless of plate content; the rig itself draws a longer explicit arm for high-five. Plates now show the true anchor geometry.

FOLLOW-UP CURE 2026-11-08 (raised-arm parts): holmes-arm-raised.png / watson-arm-raised.png are new runtime parts — the dedicated raised arm the rig draws explicitly for pose 'high-five' (DetectivePair.tsx @ 9e49da3 high-five branch: Holmes M78,58 L97,27 + hand at (99,25); Watson M36,54 L17,23 + hand at (15,21); drawn explicitly so the anchor never drifts with a rotation guess). Each part is that same arm isolated from the regenerated high-five plate, placed at its rect with NO rotation; in the high-five assembly it replaces arm-front (kid-test measurer keys on part id 'arm-raised'). Narrow-band self-check, part at rect: Holmes hand cluster 244 px, centroid (98.77,25.50) vb — 0.56 vb from (99,25); Watson 235 px, centroid (15.50,20.96) vb — 0.50 vb from (15,21). raised_arm_parts_cure.basis: Rig contract, DetectivePair.tsx @ main 9e49da3 (Holmes lines 347/425-433, Watson 511/598-606): for pose == 'high-five' ONLY the rig does NOT rotate the base arm; it draws a DEDICATED raised arm explicitly — Holmes stroke path M78,58 L97,27 (strokeWidth 10, round cap, coat colour) + hand circle at HIGH_FIVE_CONTACT (99,25) r=4.6; Watson M36,54 L17,23 + hand circle at (15,21) r=4.6. Rig comment: 'the raised hand IS the contact point, drawn explicitly so the anchor never drifts with a rotation guess.' The base arm-front palm radius (26.6 vb Holmes) cannot reach the anchor radius (39.1 vb) by any rotation, so a parts assembly that rotates arm-front reads ~7.3 rig px short through no plate defect.
raised_arm_parts_cure.method: Each part is the raised arm of the regenerated high-five pose plate, isolated (corridor + painted-register colour classes + connected component), palette-lossless (max channel delta 0 vs the plate pixels). Placed at its manifest rect with NO rotation, it replaces arm-front in the high-five assembly.
raised_arm_parts_cure.harness_detection: tests/e2e/pair-art-kidtest.spec.ts assembly section: raisedPart = parts.find(p => /high-five|highfive|raised/.test(p.part)) — the part id 'arm-raised' matches; when found, arm-front is excluded and the raised part is drawn explicitly at its rectPx with rotationDeg 0.
